title: Deep learning of lymphocyte architecture on H&E slides predicts colon cancer outcome
summary: CoATIL, a computational pathology framework, quantifies tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte spatial organization from routine H&E whole-slide images in 461 patients with microsatellite-stable or MSI-low colon adenocarcinoma. Trained on 140 patients and validated internally (n = 52) and externally in TCGA (n = 130) and a Guangdong hospital (n = 139), it was associated with progression-free survival (HR 1.32 per standard deviation, 95% CI 1.13-1.55). It was compared with a clinical model and eight foundation-model approaches; the study is retrospective and the authors state that prospective validation is warranted.
ai_technology: CoATIL computational pathology framework quantifying TIL spatial architecture from whole-slide images
organization: Georgia Institute of Technology; Emory University; The Wallace H. Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering

evidence.tested: Training in one hospital cohort with internal validation and two external validation cohorts, assessed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression.
evidence.unknown: Prospective validation; prognostic value beyond established markers in larger cohorts; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A computational pathology framework derived lymphocyte spatial features from H&E slides.
